video_title: Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady NBA Draft Watch Party Live From New York | Cousins Courtside

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa's development benefits from playing with veterans like Trae Young
quotes.excerpt: He could go to a stabilized lineup to where you have Trae Young, you have Anthony Davis.
quotes.quote: Especially your number one pick, you don't want too much pressure to be on that kid. At least he could go to a stabilized lineup to where you have Trae Young, you have Anthony Davis. These guys are veterans, can help with his development, his maturity, his maturation process. So I think that's a good landing spot for him as he progresses in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Vince Carter
quotes.summary_phrase: AJ Dybantsa's situation is similar to Cooper Flagg's arrival in the league
quotes.excerpt: I look at this situation kind of like with Cooper Flagg walked into. He has the chance
quotes.quote: I look at this situation kind of like with Cooper Flagg walked into. He has the chance to have a veteran, another number one pick on his team that can kind of show him the ropes, take some pressure off him. A lot of pressure is going to be on him because he's the number one pick, but at the same time, you can play through Anthony Davis when he's available, and he can show him the ropes to take the pressure off him where he can just be a second or third score, dare I say that.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: The anxiety of the NBA draft process is overwhelming for young players
quotes.excerpt: The anxiety, the nerves of just not knowing where your future is is right there.
quotes.quote: The anxiety, the nerves of just not knowing where your future is is right there and it's out of your control. So you're sitting there and I'm panicking and just trying to stay calm. I wasn't sick. Chicago Bulls were trying to make a trade. I don't know if anyone watched The Last Dance and they were talking about trading Scotty Pippen around that time of 1997. I was part of that. I was going to be a part of that deal. So they had called me 12 o'clock the night before the draft. I had to go shoot to the clinic, take a physical, and it was about to go down the next night. Jerry Reinsdorf and Michael Jordan axed that deal and the trade didn't go through.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: The pressure of being drafted and walking on stage at the draft
quotes.excerpt: When your name gets called, the one thing for me walking up, don't trip on these steps.
quotes.quote: When your name gets called, the one thing for me walking up, don't trip on these steps, because one, my whole body, my legs, everything is heavy because I can't believe I just got drafted, straight out of high school. So I'm already, I'm bugging. So I'm like, yo, do not trip in front of all these people in this national television. That was the only thing I was thinking about.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: The defensive limitations of Zach Edey and the need for athletic bigs
quotes.excerpt: If you have a center like Zach Edey who's slow foot on defensive side of the ball,
quotes.quote: If you have a center like Zach Edey who's slow foot on defensive side of the ball, you need your power forward to be able to cover some ground for him. Defensively, so I think you have two guys in your front court that are slow, slow foot, can't really cover that much ground. So when you're playing a team like, let's go, OKC with a bunch of shooters, San Antonio can spread you out with shooters, they can't cover that ground.

quotes.speaker: Jadakiss
quotes.summary_phrase: Biggie Smalls' advice on not being one-dimensional as an artist
quotes.excerpt: Big always told me, don't be one dimensional. If you make a C-N-I-G commercial, if you make
quotes.quote: Big always told me, don't be one dimensional. If you make a C-N-I-G commercial, if you make a song about a girl, if you make whatever, this, that, be able to do it all. Don't just be known to just do that.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: The mental impact of scoring 40 or 50 points in a game
quotes.excerpt: When I have a 40 or 50 point game, it ain't just for that night.
quotes.quote: When I have a 40 or 50 point game, it ain't just for that night. I'm waking up the next day and I feel like I'm going to get 40. The next day after that, I feel like I'm going to get 40. That shit is going to carry on for a few days. I don't know how guys hit 40 or hit a 50 point game and they come back and have 12. Are you shitting me?

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyrese Haliburton's influence on young players' development
quotes.excerpt: He got a little bit of Tyrese Haliburton in him.
quotes.quote: He got a little bit of Tyrese Haliburton in him. And he said that's kind of one of the guys he looks up to is Haliburton. So, you know, maybe now here's another guy that goes out there, can run your offense, sometimes, you know, backup right now too to Darius Garland. I mean, uh, yeah, Garland. He got good height too and he's going to put on some more size, but that what that's what he can do.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady's motivation to prove he was more than just an athlete
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to show that I was more than an athlete that I can handle the ball.
quotes.quote: I wanted to show that I was more than an athlete that I can handle the ball, that I can pass the ball and that I can shoot the ball. Because a lot of people like you say, man, I didn't know you could shoot the ball like that. And that's I heard it all the time. Even even after my days of playing, I was trying to get once, that's it. I wanted one or two steps and then upper room, baby.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady's preference for ball handling over shooting
quotes.excerpt: I would question your handles more than shooting the ball.
quotes.quote: I would question your handles more than shooting the ball like, you know, even after my days of playing. I was trying to get once, that's it. I wanted one or two steps and then upper room, baby.

quotes.speaker: Tracy McGrady
quotes.summary_phrase: Tracy McGrady's experience auditioning for the movie 'He Got Game'
quotes.excerpt: I went and cast it for the movie, right? Now, I'm fresh out of high school.
quotes.quote: I went and cast it for the movie, right? Now, I'm fresh out of high school. I don't know anything about Hollywood. I don't know anything. I'm fresh out of, you know, Florida, I'm country boy, right? Yes. I showed up in a white pinstripe suit, deck down, looking like a freaking fool, going to do an audition for He Got Game and Denzel's looking at me like, yo, what the hell you got on, bro? Because I am, I'm decked out. I look better than I did on my draft night, going for this audition, man. And it was great to see him. He told that story like a year or two ago and it was, it was pretty refreshing to see him talk about that moment because it it took me back like, I was 18 years old going to, uh, do this, this audition for this movie looking like, you know, I thought I was sharp, but he looked at me like, yo, what you got on, man? Try again, mother sucker.
